content:
# Process Rule: Wheat Brown Rust (Puccinia triticina)

**Trigger**: Orange-yellow uredinia (pustules) on upper leaf surface of wheat, possibly with yellow halos.

## Step 1 — Confirm Diagnosis
- Identify orange-yellow pustules on leaf upper surface (uredinia of Puccinia triticina)
- Check for yellow halos around pustules
- Distinguish from stripe rust (yellow pustules in rows) and stem rust (dark red-brown, on stems)
- **gateway_decision**: set diagnosis = 'Brown Rust / Puccinia triticina'

## Step 2 — Assess Severity
- LOW (<15% leaf area): monitor, scout every 5 days
- MEDIUM (15–40% leaf area): fungicide application warranted
- HIGH (>40% leaf area): urgent fungicide application

## Step 3 — Weather Check Gateway
<<decision>>
- If temperature 15–22°C AND relative humidity >80%: weather_check = YES (favorable for spread)
- If temperature >30°C or dry conditions: weather_check = NO (unfavorable, monitor only)
<<if yes>>
  Proceed to Step 4 — apply fungicide
<<if no>>
  Monitor every 5 days, reassess if weather changes
<<end>>

## Step 4 — Fungicide Application
- LOW severity: Tebuconazole 250 g/L, dose 0.4–0.6 L/ha, apply early morning
- MEDIUM severity: Tebuconazole 250 g/L, dose 0.6–0.9 L/ha, apply early morning
- HIGH severity: Propiconazole 250 EC, dose 0.8–1.0 L/ha, apply immediately
- Use get_treatment_protocol to confirm product and calculate_dosage for field area
- Respect PHI (pre-harvest interval) of 35 days for Tebuconazole

## Step 5 — Follow-up
- Scout 7–10 days after application
- Should_escalate = false unless >40% canopy affected AND no fungicide response

# Process Rule: Tomato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)

**Trigger**: Water-soaked brown-black lesions on tomato leaves with white sporulation on leaf underside under humid conditions.

## Step 1 — Confirm Diagnosis
- Water-soaked lesions expanding rapidly, turning brown-black
- White cottony sporulation on lower leaf surface in humid conditions
- Dark cankers on stems; firm brown rot on fruits
- **gateway_decision**: set diagnosis = 'Late Blight / Phytophthora infestans'

## Step 2 — Weather Check Gateway
<<decision>>
- If temperature 10–20°C AND leaf wetness >10 hours: weather_check = YES (high risk)
- If temperature >28°C or dry: weather_check = NO (lower immediate risk)
<<if yes>>
  Proceed to Step 3 — emergency fungicide application
<<if no>>
  Preventive application, monitor every 3 days
<<end>>

## Step 3 — Severity Branch Gateway
<<decision>>
- If >30% plants symptomatic: severity_branch = YES (high severity — emergency)
- If <30% plants: severity_branch = NO (moderate — standard protocol)
<<if yes>>
  Apply cymoxanil + mancozeb at maximum dose (3 kg/ha), remove heavily infected plants
<<if no>>
  Apply cymoxanil 2.0–2.5 kg/ha or metalaxyl 0.5–1.0 kg/ha, repeat every 7 days
<<end>>

## Step 4 — Cultural Controls
- Stop overhead irrigation immediately; switch to drip or base watering
- Remove and destroy infected plant material (do not compost)
- Improve air circulation
- Use get_weather to confirm current conditions
- Use get_treatment_protocol for product selection and calculate_dosage

## Step 5 — Follow-up
- Inspect every 3–4 days
- Should_escalate = false unless >50% crop loss or systemic stem infection

content:
# Process Rule: Olive Fruit Fly (Bactrocera oleae)

**Trigger**: Oviposition stings (small dark puncture marks) on olive fruits, larval tunneling inside flesh, premature fruit drop, secondary rot.

## Step 1 — Confirm Diagnosis
- Inspect for oviposition stings: small dark puncture marks on olive skin
- Cut symptomatic fruit: look for larval galleries/tunneling in flesh
- Check for adult fly activity with yellow sticky traps
- **gateway_decision**: set diagnosis = 'Olive Fruit Fly / Bactrocera oleae'

## Step 2 — Assess Infestation Level
- Sample 50 fruits per block, count infested
- LOW: <5% infested fruits
- MEDIUM: 5–20% infested fruits
- HIGH: >20% infested fruits

## Step 3 — Infestation Threshold Gateway
<<decision>>
- If infestation >5% infested fruits: infestation_threshold = YES (above economic threshold)
- If infestation <=5%: infestation_threshold = NO (below threshold — mass trapping only)
<<if yes>>
  Proceed to Step 4 — insecticide intervention
<<if no>>
  Deploy protein bait traps (ammonium acetate + yeast), monitor weekly
<<end>>

## Step 4 — Weather Check Gateway
<<decision>>
- If temperature 15–30°C: weather_check = YES (optimal for spray efficacy)
- If temperature >35°C or <10°C: weather_check = NO (delay spray, continue trapping)
<<if yes>>
  Proceed to Step 5 — spray application
<<if no>>
  Deploy/maintain traps, reassess when temperature normalises
<<end>>

## Step 5 — Harvest Proximity Gateway
<<decision>>
- If harvest within 21 days: harvest_proximity = YES (use short-PHI product)
- If harvest >21 days away: harvest_proximity = NO (standard product)
<<if yes>>
  Apply Spinosad (PHI 7 days), dose 0.3 L/ha, early morning or evening
<<if no>>
  Apply Deltamethrin (PHI 28 days), dose 0.2–0.3 L/ha; or Dimethoate for high pressure
<<end>>

## Step 6 — Cultural Controls
- Collect and destroy fallen infested fruit daily (break life cycle)
- Prune heavily infested branches
- Use get_weather to confirm application conditions
- Use get_treatment_protocol for product confirmation
- Use check_waiting_period to verify PHI compliance

## Step 7 — Follow-up
- Inspect traps and canopy every 3–5 days
- Escalate to HIGH severity protocol if symptomatic fruit >50% or trap catches increase >20%/week
- Should_escalate = false unless grove-wide epidemic (>30% trees severely infested)

trigger: wheat fusarium head blight scab Fusarium graminearum bleached spikelets tombstone kernels mycotoxin
content:
# Process Rule: Wheat Fusarium Head Blight / Scab (Fusarium graminearum)

**Trigger**: Premature bleaching/whitening of individual spikelets or entire wheat heads at anthesis; pink-orange sporodochia at spikelet base; shriveled tombstone kernels.

## Step 1 — Confirm Diagnosis
- Bleached spikelets on otherwise green heads (partial head blight)
- Pink-orange spore masses at spikelet base under wet conditions
- Shriveled, chalky kernels at grain fill stage
- **gateway_decision**: set diagnosis = 'Fusarium Head Blight / Fusarium graminearum'

## Step 2 — Weather Check Gateway
<<decision>>
- If temperature 20–25°C AND humid/rainy during anthesis (GS 60–69): weather_check = YES
- If dry conditions during flowering or temperature <15°C: weather_check = NO
<<if yes>>
  HIGH risk — proceed to Step 3
<<if no>>
  LOWER risk — monitor, apply fungicide only if symptoms appear
<<end>>

## Step 3 — Timing Critical Gateway
<<decision>>
- If wheat currently at anthesis (GS 60–69, 50% head emergence): timing_critical = YES (optimal window)
- If tillering or grain fill stage: timing_critical = NO (application less effective)
<<if yes>>
  Apply fungicide immediately — this is the most critical window
<<if no>>
  Document timing constraint; note reduced efficacy in report
<<end>>

## Step 4 — Mycotoxin Risk Gateway
<<decision>>
- If susceptible variety AND high disease pressure (>25% heads symptomatic): mycotoxin_risk = YES
- Otherwise: mycotoxin_risk = NO
<<if yes>>
  Use prothioconazole + tebuconazole at full dose (1.5 L/ha) — maximum mycotoxin reduction
<<if no>>
  Standard dose: Tebuconazole 250 g/L at 1.0–1.25 L/ha
<<end>>

## Step 5 — Fungicide Application
- LOW: Tebuconazole 250 g/L, 0.8–1.0 L/ha at anthesis
- MEDIUM: Metconazole + Tebuconazole, 1.0–1.25 L/ha, repeat in 7 days
- HIGH: Prothioconazole + Tebuconazole, 1.25–1.5 L/ha, immediate
- Apply with hollow-cone nozzle aimed at heads
- Use get_weather for current conditions, get_treatment_protocol for product, calculate_dosage
- Use check_waiting_period — PHI Tebuconazole: 35 days

## Step 6 — Follow-up
- Monitor mycotoxin levels at harvest (DON threshold: 1.25 ppm EU)
- Should_escalate = true if >50% heads symptomatic AND grain filling already initiated (irreversible yield loss)

trigger: citrus greening HLB huanglongbing Liberibacter blotchy mottle asymmetric yellowing psyllid Diaphorina citri
content:
# Process Rule: Citrus Greening / HLB (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus)

**Trigger**: Blotchy mottling on citrus leaves not following vein patterns (asymmetric); lopsided small fruits; yellow shoots; presence of psyllid vector (Diaphorina citri).

## Step 1 — Confirm Diagnosis
- Blotchy mottle: asymmetric yellowing NOT following leaf veins (unlike nutritional deficiency)
- Lopsided fruits with bitter juice and underdeveloped seeds
- Yellow flush shoots with twig/branch dieback
- Psyllid nymphs or adults on new growth
- **gateway_decision**: set diagnosis = 'Citrus Greening / HLB / Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus'

## Step 2 — Confirmation Test Gateway
<<decision>>
- If PCR test or field diagnostic kit confirms Liberibacter: confirmation_test = YES
- If test negative or pending: confirmation_test = NO
<<if yes>>
  Confirmed HLB — proceed to Step 3 eradication protocol
<<if no>>
  Treat as nutritional deficiency (Zn/Mn foliar spray), retest in 30 days
<<end>>

## Step 3 — Tree Removal Gateway
<<decision>>
- If disease incidence >30% in block: tree_removal = YES (remove infected + buffer trees)
- If incidence <30%: tree_removal = NO (intensive vector suppression)
<<if yes>>
  Remove infected trees + 2-tree buffer; immediate psyllid suppression in surrounding blocks
  Notify local plant health authority
<<if no>>
  Intensive psyllid vector suppression program (Step 4)
<<end>>

## Step 4 — Vector Pressure Gateway
<<decision>>
- If psyllid >1 nymph per flush shoot: vector_pressure = YES (high pressure)
- If psyllid <=1 nymph per flush: vector_pressure = NO (low pressure)
<<if yes>>
  Apply Spirotetramat (systemic) + Dimethoate (contact), dose 1.0–1.5 L/ha
  Repeat every 3 weeks during new flush periods
<<if no>>
  Preventive: Imidacloprid soil drench or foliar, 0.3–0.5 L/ha at flush emergence
<<end>>

## Step 5 — Nutritional Support
- All HLB-positive trees: foliar micronutrient program (Zn, Mn, B, Cu) every 6 weeks
- Maintain optimal irrigation and fertilization to slow symptom progression
- Use get_disease_info for Liberibacter confirmed distribution in region
- Use get_treatment_protocol for current-approved psyllicide
- Use check_waiting_period for PHI compliance
- Use send_sms to notify grove owner of confirmed HLB status

## Step 6 — Follow-up
- Monitor psyllid populations monthly with yellow sticky traps
- Resample disease incidence quarterly
- Should_escalate = true if incidence spreading to adjacent blocks despite interventions
